title: A reasons-first repertoire as White
origin: map-v1 (OPN.REPERTOIRE.*; the WHITE/BLACK ids are ours)

D0.outcome: Explains that a repertoire is built from the lines the learner actually meets, each ending in a model position with plans and a resulting ending.

D1.outcome: Plays the first eight moves of one reasons-first line as White, explaining each, and names the model position and the plan.

D2.outcome: Handles the three most common deviations from his own opponents' data in unlabeled positions.

D3.outcome: After twenty own games, revises the repertoire from the opponent-frequency data and writes what changed and why.

misconceptions: Choose lines by fashion, not by opponents.
sources: docs/council-synthesis.md CD-7 (repertoire driven by the learner's own opponent frequencies; spaced review only for forcing lines)
conditions: Every line ends at a model position with plans and a link to the resulting endgame.
Memory is reserved for forcing lines where one lapse loses.
Prefer simple development to a messy pawn grab when an equally good simple option exists.
contrasts: Choosing lines from theory fashion rather than the frequencies in own games.
note: Map id was OPN.REPERTOIRE.*; split into WHITE and BLACK so mastery can be tracked per colour.
